description.narrative:
Project Outcome Stakeholder effects Increased access to climate finance, including for SMEs: Southeast Asia is one of the most vulnerable regions to climate change and includes some of the most GHG intensive economies and the most exposed countries to climate disasters. The region is responsible for about 6.5 percent of global energy-related carbon dioxide emissions in 2020, a steep increase from 2.8 percent in 1990. Such unchecked growth in emissions raises the risk of raising global temperatures by 3.2 C. That in turn could cause the region's GDP to fall by up to 37 percent, according to estimates by the Swiss Re Institute . It is reported that more than 90 percent of the total GHG emissions of Southeast Asia are attributable to Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam
Market Creation: Competitiveness: IFC anticipates that the Project will promote greater competitiveness in the climate finance segment, by supporting the development of an alternate financing channel to support the development of sustainable finance. The Fund will invest in sectors that support the delivery of more efficient, competitive and sustainable technology and innovation, including in green buildings, sustainable energy, and sustainable agriculture, amongst others. Pipeline projects include a compressed biogas EPC and operator which uses biogas or bioCNG to replace natural gas to reduce GHG emission, and a smart logistics company which will contribute to GHG emissions reduction through optimizing routes and improving operational efficiency of vehicles, amongst others. Through demonstration, replication, and standard-setting channels, this is expected to lead to the future establishment of private credit funds aimed at supporting the development of sustainable solutions in Asia.

The proposed investment entails an investment of up to US$40 million for IFCs own account in a US$350 million target credit fund namely Navis Asia Credit Fund LP (NAC or the Fund). The Fund will provide senior secured loans to small to mid-sized corporates across Asia Pacific to promote sustainable financing. IFCs investment will be deployed across emerging Asia including Thailand, Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, and Indonesia. Navis Asia Credit Fund G.P. Pte. Ltd., a Singapore private company, controlled by Navis Capital Partners Limited, will serve as the general partner of the Fund (the General Partner).

name.narrative: Navis Capital Partners Limited (together with its affiliates, Navis) is headquartered in Malaysia while the main NAC investment team will be based in Singapore. As of November 2023, Navis has a team of more than 60 investment professionals spread across 7 offices in the region, including Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Hong Kong, Australia, and Indonesia. The Fund will primarily invest in emerging Asia with key markets being Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia and Philippines.
